notes.title: New "early guess" feature and new clue added
notes.content: [p]Test players for [b]Murder Is Game Over: Murder Otaku[/b] reacted positively to the new "early guess" feature where you can attempt to guess the killer before the explanation scene happens. It is an optional feature, and the correct guess results in an additional scene with a trophy. Since the feature is easy to add, I added it for [b]Murder Is Game Over: The Blackinton Curse.[/b] Also new is an additional clue to find. This just makes the story slightly improved. Hope players enjoy the game and the new content! Don't forget to check out the new one![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45093116/316154e0d622b7f66eec42507a33830d1c10d97c.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45093116/1469246f05ffc4e6377a66f5e7c07fe9bedc52a4.jpg"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Excellence In Narrative award
notes.content:
I'm extremely proud to share that Murder Is Game Over: The Blackinton Curse was selected for the "Excellence In Narrative" award at [url=www.bostonfig.com]Boston Festival of Indie Games[/url]. The judges provided wonderful feedback, and the event attendees had a lot of fun playing the game. Thanks to everyone involved for the support! All the projects at the festival were extremely high-quality, and it was a privilege to be a part of the event and be recognized.

notes.title: Official Selection - Boston Festival of Indie Games 2024
notes.content: [b]Murder Is Game Over: The Blackinton Curse[/b] is an [i]official selection[/i] at this year's [url=https://www.bostonfig.com/fest-homepage/][b]Boston Festival of Indie Games[/b][/url]! The event takes place at Cyclorama in Boston on Sunday,  December 15th, 2024. I will be on-site with a booth showcasing the game, selling and promoting, and hanging out with fans.  Excited to have my work recognized by the event organizers and praised by the critique staff! I'm looking forward to being there, and hope to see you then!

notes.title: Moving forward with Murder Is Game Over #4
notes.content:
[b]Moving forward[/b]

Ideally, I’d like to create something that combines my favorite elements of all 3 games: the open-world map layout from the first game, the memorable showdown with a powerful antagonist in the second game, and the spooky, suspenseful atmosphere of the third game. Overall I’ve been pleased with the responses to this game series and the calls to keep making more Murder Is Game Over games. Scripting games is definitely one of those things where your technical skills improve every time, but creating compelling stories is always a challenge.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45093116/d5437f945e0bc64d65a8e41e58f4fffbfdd3e745.jpg[/img]

[b](Bonus) Best music – Paladin Dream[/b]

I consider Paladin Dream to be my learning project, and it’s fairly primitive compared to what I’m capable of doing now. But the music is great. I really wanted to make a soundtrack worthy of comparison with the best RPGs and felt that there are times when that happens. I’m especially proud of the final boss battle featuring vocals and lyrics as a “religious hymn” to the story’s legendary hero character. The game may not be “important” enough for most people to take the music seriously, but that doesn’t mean the music isn’t high quality.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45093116/a117873d4886c6dd9832387a553b277c52abf448.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Murder Is Game Over Series Retrospective – Part 1
notes.content:
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/6138946/92d01e216e79e6660b894f6601cd3cc2b3ee871e.png[/img]

After developing and releasing 3 “Murder Is Game Over” titles in 2 years, I’ve had some time to pause and reflect on what I like most about each one. These are my thoughts on the series as a whole.

Best exploration – Murder Is Game Over

My initial concept for this game was to have a murder mystery that emphasized exploration much more inspired by RPGs than adventure games. In hindsight, the world design from the first game was well done in terms of giving the player freedom to move around the world at their choosing. The map shape is based on a series of interconnecting circles including the castle's ground floor, connecting the second floor and the sealed wing, and finally, a secret passage connecting the castle to the surrounding countryside. The method of murder also relies heavily on the way the map makes a seemingly inaccessible area easy to reach through a clever shortcut. Not only is the exploration mechanic effective for the player, but it also serves as part of the storytelling and narrative.
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/6138946/7f80e1fc4e2a5ded79aded636f18e96e6a8fc179.jpg[/img]

Which game in the series has my favorite villain? Find out in part 2 coming next!

I'm creating the fourth game in the series. Please wishlist it (link below). Thank you for your support!
Matt
